english: The wolf gave the piglet a pledge: "I will not eat you." The piglet [said]: "I trust (you)." But then the wolf broke the pledge and devoured him. When one is hungry, his pledge is broken.
uncertain: bʰebʰóydʰh₂e: PRF.1SG 'I am confident/trust'; object unexpressed
misfit: gʷétes: PST.2SG 'you were saying' but subject is pórḱos (3SG nominative); expected 3SG gʷétet 'the piglet said'

english: A sheep, on which there was no wool, saw horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a great load, one carrying a man swiftly.
uncertain: whole text: older non-laryngeal orthography (awis, akwams, dadarka, wagʰantam...); the analyzer recognizes nothing except 'tam'; translated from the recognizable forms
tam: analyzer reads fem ACC.SG, but here it means 'one (of them)' and refers to horses (acc pl)
misfit: whole text: written in a different reconstruction system (no laryngeals, a-vocalism) from the rest of the packet; no form analyzes in this lexicon

english: A goat was standing on a rock, and a wolf, seeing him, said: "Goat, go down to the field. It is good." [The goat said:] "You are not looking at that; you are looking at me." So the wolf left. His word is good, but his heart is hungry.
uncertain: tód ne spéḱyesi / spéḱyesi me: speaker change to the goat is unmarked
h₂éǵrom: accusative of goal 'to the field'
ḱérdih₁: analyzer gives only NOM/VOC/ACC DU; an instrumental 'hungry in heart' reading is not supported by the analyzer
misfit: ḱérdih₁: NOM/ACC DUAL 'two hearts' with singular verb kénketi; expected NOM.SG ḱḗr (or LOC ḱérdi 'hungry in heart')

english: A bear, a wolf and an eagle seized a large fish, and the bear said: "It is mine. I am strong." The wolf and the eagle (both) said: "You are strong, and we two are weak." And the two left. The strong one takes, and the weak go hungry.
A horse grew tired and lay down. "Mother Earth, take me. I carried the wheel of the sun." And Earth took him. The Earth is the mother of mortals.
uncertain: dʰéǵʰōm: NOM or ACC; tóm (masc acc, the horse) makes Earth the subject
bʰérom: PST.1SG 'I was carrying / used to carry'

english: There was a bird's nest in a tree, and a snake was crawling toward the nest, and she (the bird) became afraid and said: "Eagle, listen to me! A snake is crawling toward my nest." And the eagle, hearing her, came and seized the snake. A friend hears the one who cries out.
uncertain: ḱéywos: noun/adj 'friend, dear one' (also PRS.1DU 'we lie' - rejected)

english: An eagle seized a sheep and went up (flew off). And a bird saw that: "I too will take a ram!" And it took him, but the fleece held her fast, and the shepherd seized her. And she cried out: "I am not an eagle!" Her who is not an eagle, the shepherd seized.
uncertain: h₂éwis: NOM 'bird' (also GEN of 'sheep' - rejected); feminine, matching tā́m/séh₂
h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂: 'wool, fleece', subject of kapyét 'was gripping'

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep! Our heart pains us, having seen this: man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep has no wool."
uncertain: whole text: older non-laryngeal orthography; only 'swas' analyzes (accidentally, as swos ACC.PL); translated from recognizable forms
wiwidwant- swas: hyphen-split token 'to us having seen'
misfit: whole text: written in a different reconstruction system (no laryngeals, a-vocalism) from the rest of the packet; nothing analyzes in this lexicon

english: Two horses were pulling a wagon. The wagon said: "I carry the man." A horse said: "I pull you." The yoke said: "[It/I] join(s) those two." Then the man let the two horses go, and the wagon stood still. If the horse does not pull, the wagon stands still.
misfit: yunégti: PRS.3SG inside the yoke's quoted speech; expected 1SG yunégmi 'I join'

english: A sheep lived in a field, and a dog guarded her. Then a wolf saw her and said to her: "Sheep, the dog is not your friend. Drive him away, and I will be a friend to you." And she drove him away. And she called out: "Where is he?" Then [the wolf] devoured her. She who drives off the dog feeds the wolf.
uncertain: gʷr̥h₃ét: no subject expressed; wolf understood
só kúdʰe h₁ésti: speaker read as the sheep calling for the dog

english: A dog carrying a fish came to the water, and he saw a dog in the water: "Give me your fish!" And he barked, and it (the fish) slipped from his mouth into the water, and the water carried it away. He who seeks much loses his own.
uncertain: wédos (1st): accusative of goal 'to the water'
só: the fish (masc) as subject of h₃sléydʰt
swóm: neuter nom 'his own (thing)' as subject of intransitive néḱt 'vanished', lit. 'his own vanishes for him'

english: A snake came to the water and said to a horse: "Carry me across the water." [Horse:] "Snake, I fear you." [Snake:] "I will not kill you. If I kill you, I shall die." So the horse carried him, and the snake killed him, and both died. He who kills the one carrying him, he dies.
uncertain: mr̥tā́m: AOR.3DU 'the two died' (also ACC.SG fem of mr̥tós 'dead' - rejected)

english: A wolf was wearing wool (a fleece) and went into the field. And the shepherd, seeing him, said: "This sheep is a fine one. I shall cook her tonight." And the shepherd killed him and cooked him. He who wears that wool, the shepherd kills him.
uncertain: tā́m (fem, the 'sheep') vs tóm (masc, the wolf): deliberate contrast

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field (plain).
uncertain: h₂aǵróm: nonstandard spelling of h₂éǵrom (a-vowel, final accent); analyzer also allows GEN.PL
bʰuged: not in lexicon/analyzer; read as aorist 'fled' of bʰewg-
misfit: bʰuged: unanalyzable form (nonstandard ending/accent for bʰugét 'fled'); same older reconstruction style as 25d69709/531af602

english: Swift horses ran in a field, and the eagle, seeing them, said to them: "Horses, you go on the earth, and I go above." [Horses:] "Eagle, come down and run!" So he came down, and did not run. He who is great in the sky is not great on the earth.
uncertain: sékʷt: 'said' vs 'followed'; dative tóybʰos favors 'said to them'
ne-kʷe drémt: 'and did not / could not run'

english: A bear was driving a horse from the field, and the horse went to a man: "Man, the bear is driving me out. Drive him out!" The man said: "Take the yoke, and I will drive him out." So the horse took the yoke, and the man yoked him and drove the bear out. [Horse:] "Let me go." [Man:] "I will not let you go." He who goes to man bears the yoke.

A bear seized a mouse. The mouse said: "Let me go. I am weak and you are strong. If you let me go, I will free you." So he let him go. Then men threw a rope around the bear, and the bear cried out, and the mouse, hearing him, ran and cut that rope. [Bear:] "You freed me." The weak freed the strong.
uncertain: drémt tóm ḱl̥wónts: 'ran, hearing him' (tóm object of participle)

english: A serpent was devouring a bull, and the eagle struck the serpent down. A bird said to him: "Eagle, how is your name famous?" [Eagle:] "I killed him." He who slays the serpent, his is undying fame.
uncertain: gʷʰént: PST 'was striking' read as 'struck down'

english: Two friends were going along a road, and a bear came upon the two of them, and one of the two climbed into a tree, and the (other) friend lay down. And the bear came near and touched him (or: went away), and the one came down: "What did the bear say to you?" "He told me: do not follow that one." He who leaves you is not a friend.
uncertain: sékʷeth₂e: MID.PST.2SG with mē = prohibitive 'do not follow'
misfit: stéygʰome: PST.1PL 'we were climbing' but subject is sḿ̥teros 'one of the two' (NOM.SG) in narration; expected 3SG stéygʰet

english: Ice was covering the water in winter, and a goat was walking on the ice, and a horse came to it. The goat said to him: "Horse, do not go onto the ice. It is not strong." "Goat, I am big, and it is strong." And he went onto it, and the ice split, and the horse sank into the water. The ice holds up the weak, and it splits under the strong.
uncertain: h₁yégos: lexicon has no gloss; root 'ice, frost'
tód ... Hn̥dʰí: read 'it (ice) splits under the strong one' with ish₁róm as object of Hn̥dʰí
gʷémt ... tód: 'came to it' - referent ice or water (wódr̥, neuter) unclear
misfit: tód (x3 predicating 'it' = the ice: 'tód ish₁róm ne h₁ésti', 'tód-kʷe ish₁róm h₁ésti', 'bʰidtó-kʷe tód'): neuter pronoun for h₁yégos, which declines thematically (loc h₁yégoy) and so should be masculine; the inconsistency could also be the thematic locative if h₁yégos was meant as a neuter s-stem (same pattern in 936f2bec)

english: It was getting dark, and a serpent was searching for a piglet in the night. The piglet was praying: "Dawn, daughter of the Sky, come! Show the serpent to the dog!" And it grew light, and the dog, seeing the serpent, barked, and the serpent fled. He who goes about in the night flees at dawn.
uncertain: moldʰéyet: no lexicon gloss; root 'pray to a deity'
woydéye: causative 'make see', ḱunéy dative 'make the dog see'

english: A fish and a catfish were living in the water, and the sun was drying up the water. The fish said to him: "Catfish, the water is gone. Let us go to the lake." [Catfish:] "I dwell in my own water." So the fish swam to the lake, and the catfish died. When the water is gone, he who stays dies.

The sheep said to her daughter: "Daughter, do not go to the water at night. A she-wolf stands there." But the daughter did not heed her mother, and went to it (the water), and the she-wolf seized her, and the daughter cried: "Mother, hear me!" And the she-wolf devoured her. A mother's word saves her who heeds it.

A dog was lying in the barley, and cattle came to the cow-stall. They said to him: "Dog, you do not eat barley. Give us the barley." [Dog:] "Cows, go away! I do not give you the barley." So they pushed him out and ate up the barley. He who does not eat and does not give is pushed out.

A rope was lying on the road, and a horse looked at it and became afraid. He said: "It is a snake!" and fled. Then a snake was lying on the road, and the horse did not see the snake and stepped on it, and the snake struck him. He who fears the rope does not see the snake.

A she-wolf was drinking water upstream, and a ram was drinking downstream. She said to him: "You are drinking my water." [Ram:] "The water goes from you to me." [Wolf:] "You drank it last year." [Ram:] "Last year I was not alive." "Then your father drank my water." And she devoured him. For a hungry wolf there is a word (a pretext).
uncertain: wékʷos ... h₁ésti: 'there is a word' = an excuse
misfit: tód (in 'tód péruti píph₃es'), low confidence: neuter pronoun for h₂ékʷeh₂ 'water', which is feminine (expected tā́m); could be abstract 'that (is what) you did'

english: Four cattle were standing under a tree, and the serpent was watching them. "Cattle, give me one of you." "We stand (together), and we do not give you one." So he left. Then one went to the water away from the cattle, and the serpent seized him and devoured him. The serpent kills him who leaves the herd.
misfit: h₁ógʷʰih₁: NOM/ACC DUAL 'two serpents' with 3SG spéḱyet, and later singular h₁ógʷʰis; expected NOM.SG h₁ógʷʰis

english: A bear was lying in winter (sleep), and the ice was melting. A bird in the tree called: "Wake up! It is melting." And he woke and said: "I am hungry," and stood up. When the ice melts, the bear wakes.
misfit: tód (in 'tód tinéh₁ti'): neuter pronoun for h₁yégos 'ice', a thematic (masculine) noun; expected só
